## Automated Status Summary
#### Scope
In tools/embedding_provider.py lines 155 and 214, both OpenAIEmbeddingProvider.embed and LocalFallbackEmbeddingProvider.embed filter input texts using list comprehensions: items = [text.strip() for text in texts if text and text.strip()]. When a caller provides an iterable containing empty or whitespace-only strings (e.g. ["text", "", "more"]), dropping elements changes the returned vector count (len(response.vectors) != len(texts)), corrupting positional 1-to-1 alignment between input documents and output embedding vectors.

#### Tasks
- [x] Update OpenAIEmbeddingProvider.embed in tools/embedding_provider.py to preserve input sequence length
- [x] Update LocalFallbackEmbeddingProvider.embed in tools/embedding_provider.py to return a zero or fallback vector for empty items
- [x] Add unit tests in tests/test_main.py asserting len(resp.vectors) == len(texts) for inputs containing empty strings

#### Acceptance criteria
- [x] `pytest tests/test_main.py` passes with all tests green.
- [x] `python -c "from tools.embedding_provider import LocalFallbackEmbeddingProvider; p = LocalFallbackEmbeddingProvider(); r = p.embed(['a', '', 'b']); assert len(r.vectors) == 3"` succeeds.
- [x] Deliberate-break demonstration: re-introducing the if text.strip() filter causes `pytest tests/test_main.py` to fail on empty-item test cases, and reverting restores pass.

<!-- auto-status-summary:end -->

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

- **Bug Fixes**
  - Embedding results now consistently preserve the original input order.
  - Blank or whitespace-only inputs receive zero vectors while maintaining the configured dimensions.
  - Mixed inputs continue to produce one result per input, including entries filtered before processing.
  - Embedding responses now report detected vector dimensions in their metadata.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Opener recovery validation

Rebased onto current main and fixed the optional-dimension type assertions. Mocked OpenAI tests now cover mixed blank inputs, all-blank inputs, empty input, iterator input, exact vector positions, and retained nonblank text stripping. `python3 -m pytest tests/test_main.py -q`: 10 passed. `python3 -m mypy --follow-imports=silent --ignore-missing-imports tests/test_main.py`: passes; the prior tests reproduced three operator errors. Ruff and Black pass. Restoring input filtering causes four alignment tests to fail; byte restoration returns all ten to pass. The issue alignment one-liner passes.

Whitespace review finding: main already calls `text.strip()` before OpenAI embedding. Retaining stripping preserves existing behavior; the new mocked test locks this down. Active review threads require reviewer disposition; no self-resolution or merge is claimed.

<!-- pr-preamble:start -->
<!-- meta:issue:554 -->
> **Source:** Issue #554

Closes #554

<!-- pr-preamble:end -->

<!-- auto-status-summary:start -->
## Automated Status Summary
#### Scope
`research-program/artifacts/work-bundle/` is prepared to be handed to colleagues in the owner's work environment, and the rest of `research-program/` is published to a public repository. Two disclosure-class defects have already reached this tree, both invisible on a casual read:

- A credential scan printed token prefixes into a working file before it was caught by hand.
- A batch of issue bodies carried a drafting agent's private working-directory paths (`[LOCAL_WORKSPACE]/<Repo>/...`), which made twenty-two issues unactionable across the fleet and had to be repaired one by one.

Both were found by a person looking. Neither would have been caught by any check in this repository, because there is none. The bundle's own redaction pass is a one-time human-reviewed step, not a gate, so nothing prevents the next artifact from reintroducing what the last one removed.

Evidence: `research-program/artifacts/work-bundle/REDACTIONS.md` records the manual redaction pass and its scope reduction; `README.md` states the disclosure standard this issue enforces; `research-program/CHECKPOINT.md` records the repair of the path-citation defect.

#### Tasks
- [x] Add `scripts/check_publication_safety.py` scanning every file under `research-program/` for: an absolute home path (`[LOCAL_HOME]/`), a credential prefix (`[REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]`, `[REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]`, `[REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]`, `[REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]`, `[REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]`, `[REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]`, `[REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]`), a private-key header (`[PRIVATE_KEY_HEADER]`, `[PRIVATE_KEY_HEADER]`), a scratchpad or drafting-agent path (`[LOCAL_WORKSPACE]/`, `[LOCAL_WORKSPACE]/`, `[LOCAL_WORKSPACE]/`), and an internal hostname pattern (`[LOCAL_HOST]` or a bare `localhost:` port reference).
- [x] Report every hit in one pass with file, line number and which rule matched; do not stop at the first.
- [x] Support an explicit allowlist file, `research-program/.publication-allow`, holding one `path:rule` pair per line with a required trailing comment giving the reason, so a deliberate exception is visible and justified rather than a silent skip.
- [x] Exit non-zero on any unallowed hit; print a summary line naming the counts for every rule including the zeros, so a clean run is distinguishable from a run that scanned nothing.
- [x] Print the number of files scanned, so a guard that matched nothing because it walked the wrong directory is visible.
- [x] Add `.github/workflows/publication-guard.yml` running the script on pull requests and on pushes to the default branch.
- [x] Add `tests/test_publication_safety.py` with fixtures for each rule, an allowlisted exception, and a clean tree.

#### Acceptance criteria
- [x] `python scripts/check_publication_safety.py` exits non-zero on a fixture containing a token prefix and names the file, the line and the rule.
- [x] The same fixture allowlisted with a reason exits zero, and an allowlist entry without a reason is itself an error.
- [x] A clean tree exits zero and prints the per-rule counts including zeros and the number of files scanned.
- [x] Pointing the scanner at an empty directory fails rather than passing, because zero files scanned is not evidence of safety.
- [x] The workflow runs on pull requests and blocks merge on failure.

<!-- auto-status-summary:end -->

<!-- workflow-source:local_request -->
Ready's default branch is red: the format check fails with `39 files would be reformatted`, all of them under `research-program/artifacts`.

That tree is not source. It is a published mirror of a local engine directory, rsynced in with deletion enabled on every worker tick, holding agent-generated scripts and reports. Formatting them would be churn the next sync discards, and the repository README already records the tree as machine-owned.

`ruff` already excludes exactly this path via `extend-exclude`. `black` did not, so the two linters disagreed about what counts as this repository's code. This adds the matching exclusion, using `force-exclude` because CI passes explicit paths and `extend-exclude` does not apply to those.

Verified locally: `black --check .` now reports 74 files unchanged, none reformatted.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
